title: Lazily delete map elements for delta metrics to re-use storage.
body:
Fixes https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8284

Currently, collection for delta metrics clears the entire sync.Map. Subsequent measurements to the same attribute sets require allocations to re-build the state that existed previously. Since this happens for the entire SDK all at once, collection can cause spikes in latency for measurements when collect happens.

The idea behind this prototype is to try and implement a version of the limitedSyncMap that doesn't immediately delete the underlying data points from the sync.Map right away.  Instead, it keeps the previous map elements around for two collection intervals before removing them.

I wrote a benchmark for DeltaSum that compares repeated Measure calls, with Measure + (fake) Collect, and just (fake) Collect.  This shows that **the measurement call after a collect takes an extra ~32 ns** (90 - 26 - 32) compared with a "regular" measurement. It also has no allocations, as we would expect by re-using the exisitng data structures.

```
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/internal/aggregate
cpu: AMD EPYC 7B12
                                       │ sdk/metric/internal/aggregate/delta_bench.txt │
                                       │                    sec/op                     │
DeltaSum/limited/MeasureNoCollect-24                                      33.68n ± 21%
DeltaSum/limited/MeasureWithCollect-24                                    350.8n ±  9%
DeltaSum/limited/OnlyCollect-24                                           109.6n ±  5%
DeltaSum/lazy/MeasureNoCollect-24                                         32.71n ±  3%
DeltaSum/lazy/MeasureWithCollect-24                                       90.52n ± 17%
DeltaSum/lazy/OnlyCollect-24                                              26.54n ± 41%
geomean                                                                   68.33n

                                       │ sdk/metric/internal/aggregate/delta_bench.txt │
                                       │                     B/op                      │
DeltaSum/limited/MeasureNoCollect-24                                      0.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/limited/MeasureWithCollect-24                                    296.0 ± 0%
DeltaSum/limited/OnlyCollect-24                                           160.0 ± 0%
DeltaSum/lazy/MeasureNoCollect-24                                         0.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/lazy/MeasureWithCollect-24                                       0.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/lazy/OnlyCollect-24                                              0.000 ± 0%
geomean                                                                              ¹
¹ summaries must be >0 to compute geomean

                                       │ sdk/metric/internal/aggregate/delta_bench.txt │
                                       │                   allocs/op                   │
DeltaSum/limited/MeasureNoCollect-24                                      0.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/limited/MeasureWithCollect-24                                    4.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/limited/OnlyCollect-24                                           1.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/lazy/MeasureNoCollect-24                                         0.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/lazy/MeasureWithCollect-24                                       0.000 ± 0%
DeltaSum/lazy/OnlyCollect-24                                              0.000 ± 0%
geomean                                                                              ¹
¹ summaries must be >0 to compute geomean
```

The additional ~35 ns is because we always acquire a lock when updating the len of the lazyLimitedSyncMap or limitedSyncMap.  We might be able to get this down to 10-15 ns if we were able to use an atomic counter.  I've tried that in the past, and haven't been able to perfectly prevent overflows in that case.

Most of this was written by Gemini
